data.label: Accounting and Auditing
data.description: The business prepares accounts, files tax returns or audits financial statements for clients. This includes accountancy practices, bookkeepers, tax advisers and audit firms.

data.label: Agricultural Equipment and Supplies
data.description: The business sells or rents farm machinery, tools, seed, feed or fertilizer to growers. It supplies farms; it does not grow the produce.

data.label: Agricultural Products
data.description: The business grows, or buys and sells, crops, livestock or other raw farm produce. It handles the produce itself, not the equipment used to grow it.

data.label: Aircraft and Maritime Vessels
data.description: The business sells, charters or maintains aircraft, boats or ships. This includes aircraft dealers, yacht brokers and marine dealers.

data.label: Animal Shelters
data.description: The organization houses stray, rescued or unwanted animals and finds new homes for them.

data.label: Art and Antiquities
data.description: The business buys, sells or auctions art, antiques or collectable objects. This includes galleries, art dealers, auction houses and agents who arrange private sales.

data.label: Automobile Dealerships
data.description: The business sells new or used cars and light vehicles to the public. It may also take vehicles in trade-in and arrange finance.

data.label: Bakeries
data.description: The business bakes bread, cakes or pastries and sells them, usually from its own store.

data.label: Bookstores
data.description: The business sells books to the public, in a store or online. It does not produce the books.

data.label: Casinos and Gambling
data.description: The business takes bets or runs games of chance for money. This includes casinos, betting shops, lotteries, online gambling sites and sports betting.

data.label: Child Care Services
data.description: The business looks after young children during the day, at a nursery, a daycare center or a home daycare.

data.label: Construction and Development
data.description: The business builds, renovates or fits out buildings and other structures, or prepares land for building. It does the construction work itself.

data.label: Credit Card Companies (Issuers & Merchant Services)
data.description: The business issues payment cards to cardholders, or signs up merchants to accept card payments. This is card issuing and merchant acquiring, not the day-to-day processing of each payment.

data.label: Crowdfunding Platforms
data.description: The business operates a platform that collects money from many people to fund a project, a loan or a company, and it holds or moves that money. A business that only raises money for itself on someone else's platform is not this subject.

data.label: Dry Cleaning and Laundry
data.description: The business cleans, presses or launders clothes and fabrics for customers.

data.label: E-commerce (General)
data.description: The business sells its own everyday goods to customers online. It owns the goods it sells, unlike a marketplace that lists other people's goods.

data.label: Educational Institutions
data.description: The organization teaches students on a formal course of study and usually awards a qualification. This includes schools, colleges and universities.

data.label: Electronics Retail
data.description: The business sells consumer electronics to the public, such as phones, computers, televisions and audio equipment.

data.label: Entertainment Industry
data.description: The business produces or promotes live entertainment, film, music or performances, or manages the people who perform.

data.label: Fast Food Establishments
data.description: The business sells prepared food and drink over a counter, for customers to take away or to eat quickly on site.

data.label: Fintech Companies
data.description: The business supplies financial products through technology, such as a lending, budgeting, payments or banking app. Its core product is software or a technology platform.

data.label: Fitness and Gym Facilities
data.description: The business runs a gym, a fitness studio or a health club where members train or exercise.

data.label: Food and Beverage Industry
data.description: The business makes, processes or wholesales food and drink products. It supplies the trade rather than serving the public directly.

data.label: Freight Forwarding and Shipping
data.description: The business arranges the transport of goods for other companies, and handles the booking, the paperwork and the customs formalities.

data.label: Funeral Services
data.description: The business arranges funerals, burials or cremations, and cares for the deceased.

data.label: General Retail
data.description: The business sells a wide mix of everyday goods to the public, with no single specialist product line.

data.label: Government Contractors
data.description: The business supplies goods, services or facilities to government bodies under a public contract. It is a private supplier to the public sector, not part of it.

data.label: Health Care Providers
data.description: The business treats patients. This includes medical practices, clinics, hospitals, dentists and other qualified health professionals.

data.label: Home Goods Retail
data.description: The business sells furniture, homeware, soft furnishings and other goods for the home.

data.label: Hospitality and Hotels
data.description: The business gives paid short-stay accommodation to guests, such as a hotel, a hostel or a guest house. Many also serve food and drink.

data.label: Import/Export and Cross-border Trade
data.description: The business buys goods in one country and sells them in another. This includes trading houses, commodity traders and import or export agents.

data.label: Insurance Providers
data.description: The business sells or underwrites insurance cover, or acts as a broker or an agent between the insurer and the customer.

data.label: IT Services and Software Development
data.description: The business writes software, or designs, builds and supports computer systems for clients.

data.label: Janitorial Services
data.description: The business cleans buildings and premises for other organizations, usually under a regular contract.

data.label: Landscaping Services
data.description: The business designs, plants or maintains gardens, grounds and other outdoor spaces.

data.label: Legal Services
data.description: The business gives legal advice or represents clients in legal matters. This includes law firms, individual lawyers and notaries.

data.label: Libraries and Museums
data.description: The organization keeps a collection of books, records or objects and lets the public consult or view it. It preserves and exhibits the collection; it does not trade in it.

data.label: Local Transportation Providers
data.description: The business carries passengers on short journeys inside one town or city area. This includes taxis, private-hire cars, shuttle buses and local transit routes.

data.label: Luxury Vehicles
data.description: The business sells premium, exotic or collectable cars. It differs from an ordinary car dealership in the price and the rarity of each vehicle.

data.label: Manufacturing
data.description: The business makes finished goods in a factory or a workshop, from raw materials or parts.

data.label: Media and Publishing
data.description: The business produces news, articles or other content and publishes it in print, online or on air. This includes newspapers, magazines and broadcasters.

data.label: Mobile Network Operators
data.description: The business runs a mobile telephone network and sells airtime or data plans to subscribers. It owns or controls the radio network itself.

data.label: Non-luxury Clothing Retail
data.description: The business sells everyday clothing and accessories at ordinary mainstream prices.

data.label: Non-Profit Organizations (NPOs)
data.description: The organization works for a public or a member benefit and does not pay profits to owners. It is usually funded by donations, grants or membership fees.

data.label: Office Supply Stores
data.description: The business sells stationery, paper, printing supplies and other goods used in an office.

data.label: Offshore Financial Services
data.description: The business supplies banking, investment or corporate financial services to clients in other countries, from a jurisdiction chosen for its tax or privacy rules. A typical sign is that almost none of its clients are in the country where it is registered.

data.label: Online Marketplaces (High-value goods)
data.description: The business runs a website where other sellers list high-value goods, such as vehicles, jewelry, watches or art, and buyers purchase them. The platform hosts the sale; it does not own the goods.

data.label: Personal Care Services
data.description: The business gives personal grooming or beauty treatments, such as hairdressing, nail care, beauty therapy or massage.

data.label: Personal Electronics Repair
data.description: The business repairs phones, computers and other consumer electronic devices.

data.label: Pharmaceuticals
data.description: The business makes or wholesales medicines and drug products, and supplies them to pharmacies, hospitals or other trade buyers. It does not treat patients.

data.label: Precious Metals and Stones
data.description: The business trades in gold, silver, platinum, diamonds or other precious stones. This includes bullion dealers, metal refiners, gemstone traders and jewelry wholesalers.

data.label: Private Banking
data.description: The business supplies banking, credit and investment management to wealthy individuals and families, one client relationship at a time. It is not banking sold to the general public.

data.label: Private Investment Funds
data.description: The business pools money from investors into a fund that is not offered to the general public. This includes hedge funds, private equity funds and venture capital funds.

data.label: Professional Training Services
data.description: The business gives short work-related training or professional courses to adults and companies. It does not run a formal academic program.

data.label: Public Administration
data.description: The organization is a government body, an agency or a public authority that delivers public services or administers public functions.

data.label: Publishing Houses
data.description: The business selects, produces and sells books. It works with authors and brings the finished book to market.

data.label: Real Estate
data.description: The business buys, sells, rents or manages property, or acts as an agent in property deals. This includes real estate agencies, property developers, landlords and property managers.

data.label: Religious Organizations
data.description: The organization is a church, a mosque, a temple or another religious body that holds worship and serves its congregation.

data.label: Retail Banking
data.description: The business takes deposits from, and lends to, the general public and small businesses, through branches or an app. It serves ordinary customers, not only wealthy ones.

data.label: Securities Brokers and Dealers
data.description: The business buys and sells shares, bonds or other securities for clients, or trades them on its own account. This includes brokerages and dealing desks.

data.label: Social Assistance Services
data.description: The organization gives non-medical help to people in need, such as counselling, food aid, housing support or community services.

data.label: Sports and Recreation Facilities
data.description: The business runs a place where people play sport or take part in leisure activities, such as a sports center, a field, a court or a swimming pool.

data.label: Supermarkets and Grocery Stores
data.description: The business sells food and household goods to the public from a grocery store or a supermarket.

data.label: Telecommunications
data.description: The business supplies telephone, internet or data communication services, or the network that carries them. A business that runs its own mobile radio network is a mobile network operator instead.

data.label: Transportation Services
data.description: The business carries passengers or goods for hire, over local or longer distances. This includes car services, bus operators and general road transport.

data.label: Travel Agencies
data.description: The business books travel, accommodation and vacations for customers. Some also package and sell their own trips as a tour operator.

data.label: Trust and Company Service Providers (TCSPs)
data.description: The business forms or administers companies, trusts or foundations for clients. It also acts as a director, a trustee, a shareholder or a registered address on a client's behalf.

data.label: Utilities (Electricity, Gas, Water)
data.description: The business generates, distributes or supplies electricity, gas or water to customers.

data.label: Veterinary Services
data.description: The business treats animals. This includes veterinary practices and animal clinics.

data.label: Waste Management
data.description: The business collects, transports, treats or disposes of waste, or runs recycling operations.

data.label: Other
data.description: The main industry of the business is not in this list. Pick this only when no other industry fits, and then describe the real activity in the follow-up question.
